Author: G.Shyam Prasad

 Hon'Ble Sri Justice G.Shyam Prasad
 Criminal Petition No.6707 of 2019
Order:

This petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short, 'the Cr.P.C.'), seeking to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.519 of 2019 on the file of the Court of Additional Judicial 1st Class Magistrate, Chodavaram, Visakhapatnam District, against the petitioners / Accused Nos.1 and 2.
2.

entities.text: Additional Judicial 1st Class Magistrate, Chodavaram, Visakhapatnam District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Petitioner No.1 is resident of Anandapuram Village, K.Kotapadu Mandal of Visakhapatnam District, running Kirana shop business and petitioner No.2 is resident of Rajupathrunipalem village,
Kothavalasa Mandal of Vizianagaram District, running Kirana shop business.

On 25.10.2018, on credible information, a raid was conducted on the Kirana shops of the petitioners 1 and 2 by the police and they found 1) Miraj premium tobacco 04 bags x 60 pouches x 15 packets, each Rs.10/-
total 3,600 packets worth Rs.36,000/-, 2) Miraj Premium tobacco 01 bag x 60 pouches x 15 packets,
total 900 packets each Rs.10/- worth Rs.9,000/-,
3) Miraj premium tobacco 01 bag x 240 pouches x 15 packets each worth Rs.5/- and 15 pouches x 15 packets, total 3825 packets worth Rs.19,125/-, 40 Deluxe mix 04 boxes x 25 packets x 50 packets &
10 packets x 50 packets each packet Rs.1/- total packets 5,500 worth Rs.5,500/- and 5) Raja tobacco 02 boxes x 40 pouches x 15 packets each Rs.5/- total 12 packets worth Rs.6,000/- (All worth Rs.75,625/-).

entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
On completion of investigation, after getting the chemical analysis report, the Section of law was altered from Section 273 I.P.C and Section 22 r/w 5(1) of COTP Act into Sections 270 and 273 I.P.C and filed charge sheet against the petitioners / Accused 1 and 2.
3.
The provisions under Sections 270 I.P.C deals with malignant act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life.
Section 273 I.P.C deals with sale of noxious food or drink.
4. The petitioners were charged for the offences punishable under Sections 270 and 273 I.P.C.

The charge sheet has been filed before the learned Magistrate and cognizance was taken and case was registered as C.C. No.519 of 2019 on the file of the Court of Additional Judicial 1st Class Magistrate,
Chodavaram, Visakhapatnam District and the trial yet to be commenced.

5. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Public Prosecutor.
Learned counsel for the petitioners placing reliance on the judgments in Criminal Petition No.6036 V Ayyappa vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 30 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32304155/
1 of 2019 and Crl.P.No.5421 of 2019 and batch on the file of this Court, submits that the police are not authorized to register crime and investigate the same, and file a charge sheet against the accused in respect of tobacco products, as the tobacco products would not fall within the purview of Indian Penal Code.
6.

entities.text: Criminal Petition No.6036 V Ayyappa vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner placed reliance on the earlier judgment of this Court in Crl.P.Nos. 3731 of 2018 and batch and submits that this Court has taken a view in respect of Section 270 I.P.C as held in unnumbered Paragraph which reads as under:
"According to Section 33 of I.P.C, the word 'act' denotes as well a series of acts as a single act; the work 'omission' denotes as well a series of omissions as a single omission.
Thus, it means, anything done by any of the persons.

Transportation of Khaini, Pan Masala or chewing tobacco itself would not spread any infection or disease and if the khaini is chewed, it may cause danger to health of any individual,
but transportation will not spread any infection or disease dangerous to health.

Therefore, the allegations made in the complaint i.e. transportation of chewing tobacco or Khaini or Pan Masala also do not constitute an offence punishable under Section 270 of I.P.C.
7.

It is appropriate to refer the provisions of Section 270 of I.P.C, which reads as under:
"According to section 270 of Indian penal code, Whoever malignantly does any act which is, and which he knows or has reason to believe to be, likely to spread the infection of any disease dangerous to life, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both".
8.

This Court has interpreted section 270 of I.P.C in the light of facts and circumstances of this case that the transportation of tobacco is not an offence as it does not spread infection or any disease dangerous to life.

9. Section 273 of I.P.C deals with sale of noxious food or drink, which reads as under:
"According to section 273 of Indian penal code, Whoever sells, or offers or exposes for sale, as food or drink, any article which has been rendered or has become noxious,
or is in a state unfit for food or drink, knowing or having reason to believe that the same is noxious as food or drink, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both".
10.

Learned counsel referred to the Crl.Petition No.3731 of 2018 and batch at unnumbered Paragraph, which reads as under:
V Ayyappa vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 30 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32304155/
2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "The other offence allegedly committed by the petitioners is punishable under Section 273 I.P.C, which deals with punishment for sale, offers or exposes for sale food or any article which has been rendered or has become noxious.
The work 'noxious' is not defined in I.P.C.
As per the dictionary meaning, noxious means harmful, deleterious, injurious and poisonous.
Therefore, the sale or offers or exposes for sale of Pan Masala, chewing tobacco or khaini are the prohibited products under the Cigarette and other Tobacco Products Act, 2003 (for short 'COTP Act').

entities.text: Cigarette and other Tobacco Products Act, 2003
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 'Transportation' of such noxious food is not included in the offence punishable under Section 273 of I.P.C, only few acts were included i.e., sale of noxious food or drink is an offence.

11. Learned counsel further submits that the police are not competent to take cognizance for the offences punishable under Sections 270 and 273 of I.P.C., as there is special enactment in respect of the products seized in this case covered under COTPA Act.

12. The Food, Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'FSS Act'), Section 41 deals with the power to warrant and authorization, 42 deals with power of entry, search, seizure and arrest without warrant of authority.

It provides that the Designated Officer, after scrutiny of the report of Food Analyst shall decide as to whether the contravention is punishable with imprisonment or fine only and in the case of contravention punishable with imprisonment, he shall send his recommendations within 14 days to Commissioner of Food Safety for sanctioning prosecution.
In case the contravention is punishable with fine only, he shall himself adjudicate and dispose of the case.

It also provides that the Commissioner of Food Safety shall, if he so deems fit, decide within the prescribed period as per the gravity of offence, whether the matter be referred to a Court of ordinary jurisdiction in case of offences punishable with imprisonment for a term up to three years, or a Special Court in case of offences punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding three years where such Special Court is established and in case no Special Court is established, such cases shall be tried by a Court of ordinary jurisdiction.
13.

The procedure of investigation by police is given as per the commentary in Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 which reads as under:
Investigation by police: for adulteration of food or misbranding, after coming into force of the provisions of FSSA vide notification dated 29th July, 2010, the authorities can take action only under the FSSA as it postulates an over riding effects over all other food related law including the PFA Act.

In view of the specific provisions under the FSSA, the offences relating to adulteration of food that are governed under the FSSA after July, 29, 2010 are to be treated as per the procedures to be followed for drawing and analysis of samples as have been provided for.
The provisions of penalties and prosecution have also been provided therein.

Therefore,
before launching any prosecution against an alleged offence of food adulteration, it is necessary for the concerned authorities to follow the mandatory requirements as provided under Sections 41 and 42 of the FSSA and, therefore, the police have no authority or jurisdiction to investigate the matter under FSSA.

Section 42 empowers V Ayyappa vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 30 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32304155/
3 the Food Safety Officer for inspection of food business, drawing samples and sending them to Food Analyst for analysis.

entities.text: V Ayyappa vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The designated Officer, after scrutiny of the report of Food Analyst shall decide as to whether the contravention is punishable with imprisonment or fine only and in the case of contravention punishable with imprisonment, he shall send his recommendations to the Commissioner of Food Safety for sanctioning prosecution.
Therefore, invoking Sections 272 and 273 of the Indian Penal Code in the matter relating to adulteration of food is wholly unjustified and non est".

14. On considering the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner and the judgments relied on the provisions of the FSS Act, 2006 it is obvious that the police cannot take cognizance of the offences pertaining to Food particularly where a special enactment is there making a provision under Sections 41 and 42 of the FSS Act, 2006.

When there is a special enactment which provides for such procedure of finding adulteration of food or misbranding a test is to be conducted, that is possible only by the concerned officials under Sections 41 and 42 of the FSS Act, 2006.

15. In the light of the facts and circumstances of this case, since the products alleged to have been seized by the police are tobacco products and in the light of the above judgments and the provisions under Sections 41 and 42 of the FSS Act, 2006, the police have no jurisdiction.

Section 3(j) of the FSS Act, in the judgment referred above, read that clearly "Therefore, in view of the law declared in various judgments referred supra, chewing tobacco and khaini are not the food within the specific definition of Section 39j) of FSS Act and the manufacture, sale or exposing for sale of tobacco etc., is governed by the provisions of COTPA Act, but not by FSS Act and so also the provisions of IPC".
16.
Therefore, it was held that respondents were incompetent to investigate the offences under Sections 54 and 59(1) of FSS Act, 2006.
The learned Public Prosecutor submits that the facts in this case are covered by the judgment in Crl. Petition No.3731 and batch.

17. In view of foregoing reasons, the Criminal Petition is allowed quashing the proceedings in C.C.No.519 of 2019, on the file of Additional Judicial 1st Class Magistrate, Chodavaram,
Visakhapatnam District, against the petitioners / Accused Nos.1 and 2.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending, shall also stand closed.
______________________ G.SHYAM PRASAD,J Date: 30.12.2019 KA V Ayyappa vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 30 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32304155/
